explanation: In August 1911 the Congress filled an office with few powers and one large one. The president appointed and dismissed ministers. In January 1915 Arriaga used that power against the Chamber. He dismissed the Democratic government and called General Pimenta de Castro, who governed with parliament suspended. The argument is about the office as much as the man. The 1911 settlement left a legal route by which a president could set the parliamentary majority aside, and Arriaga was the first to use it.
